title: Two-prover one-round games with q^6 answers and strong 4/q soundness
author: Subhash Khot and Muli Safra
work: A Two-Prover One-Round Game with Strong Soundness
source_version: Theory of Computing volume 9 article 28 (2013), official complete journal PDF acquired 2026-09-30; canonical DOI 10.4086/toc.2013.v009a028 verified against official landing and printed PDF header
difficulty_reason: After named gap-hardness/parallel-repetition and ordinary Fourier prerequisites, the proof must make virtual Hadamard subcodes cover the global code almost uniformly via the full Hellinger calculation at992–1098, and transfer local point-subspace acceptance to side-condition-respecting global Fourier lists at1123–1300. The composed proof at1303–1432 still has to identify shared virtual-table positions and convert those lists into consistent outer strategies while maintaining the q^6-alphabet and4/q soundness bounds. These complete new covering, local-to-global and composition obligations form one conservative H2 task above a direct PCP theorem invocation or routine Fourier exercise.

source_check.method: Root-approved native material plus fresh exact source0 union/body replay and24 primary/core bindings; no mathematical referee
source_check.note: Exact original Main Theorem1.2 only: for any fixed prime q>=5 and constant zeta>0, NP-hardness of distinguishing 2P1R games with R=q^6 answers and value at least1-zeta versus at most4/q. Full authored q/q^6 query-alphabet overview, projection/repetition and 3LIN definitions and named gap theorems, Fourier and Hellinger conventions, new repeated outer game and full subcode-covering calculation/parameters, complete Gowers and side-condition tests, point-subspace soundness proof and composed-PCP table identification/list-decoding closing are retained. Named Håstad 3LIN hardness, Raz-Holenstein-Rao parallel repetition, ordinary finite-field Fourier/Parseval, convexity and Hellinger inequalities are prerequisites; all new local covering, inner-test and composition material is supplied. Growing-field and quadratic-programming claims are unselected and uncounted. All-page source/output QA completed and exact final actual logs checked. Source-material candidate only; no admission/remote-delivery credit. Root admitted this exact original authored material as one H2 unit; source quirks retained unchanged.
